Best wishes,
Dave

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Difference Between Edgelist and Sociomatrix
messages.body_plain:
I'm having a problem that I can't seem to understand.

I'm creating a two-mode network, in which the actors are mailing list
members and the events are threads.  I create the network from an
edgelist, where the source node is the member participating in a
thread, and the target not is the thread.  The problem I'm having is
that it seems like the network is losing edges when I convert it back
to a sociomatrix.

> net = network(dat[,c('names','thread')])
> net2 = as.sociomatrix(net)
> network.size(net)
[1] 115
> dim(net2)
[1] 115 115
> network.edgecount(net)
[1] 373
> sum(net2)
[1] 244
> table(net2)
net2
    0     1
12981   244

So it seems to me like my sociomatrix has 129 fewer edges.

Thanks,
Sam

-- 
Sam Stewart, MMath, A.Stat

Halifax, NS, Canada, B3H 1W5

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Difference Between Edgelist and Sociomatrix
messages.body_plain:
Hi Sam.  It's hard to diagnose without having an example that will  
replicate the same problem, but here's one possibility illustrated by  
a small test case:

 > e = matrix(1:2,5,2,byrow=T)
 > e
      [,1] [,2]
[1,]    1    2
[2,]    1    2
[3,]    1    2
[4,]    1    2
[5,]    1    2

So this edgelist has 5 "edges" even though they're not all unique.  If  
we now create a network from this edgelist, the network will have 5  
edges even though the derived sociomatrix will have only one:

 > network.edgecount(network(e))
[1] 5
 > sum(as.sociomatrix(network(e)))
[1] 1

This is not a bug, by the way; there are certainly cases in which it's  
conceivable that edges could be multiple, and the network package code  
tries to be as flexible as possible.

One way to test whether this is what's causing your behavior is to  
find the number of unique rows in your edgelist as in:
 > NROW(unique(e))
[1] 1

So if you type
NROW(unique(dat[,c('names','thread')])
and get 244, that's almost certainly the explanation.

Hope this helps,
Dave

messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] edge.col does not work as expected when plotting network objects
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have just installed R and statnet on my new Linux system, but I have 
problems when I try to run some lines of code which worked without any 
problem just last week before updating the installation.

Specifically, I am not able to plot networks with custom edge colors if 
the color is given as a string. Here is an example:

 > plot(network, edge.col="gray")

returns the warning message: "In is.na(NULL) : is.na() applied to 
non-(list or vector) of type 'NULL'". Moreover, edges seem to be 
invisible in the diagram. The vertex color argument does not seem to be 
affected, so vertex.col="gray" works as expected.

If I use "edge.col=8" instead, there is no problem. Actually I would 
like to use custom shades of gray (in my case, "gray44") though, so I 
would prefer not to convert the color strings to integers.

Any ideas what could have caused this problem or how I can solve it?

Thanks and have a nice Sunday,

Philip

--

object. I have a directed edgelist with unique and non-sequential vertex IDs
(14 digit identifiers) and a matrix with the same unique and non-sequential
vertex IDs and attributes. I convert the edgelist into a network object with
sequential IDs with the following code.

el=read.csv(file.choose(),header=F)
code=sort(unique(c(el[,1],el[,2])))
el[,1]=match(el[,1],code)
el[,2]=match(el[,2],code)
n=network(el,matrix.type="edgelist",directed=FALSE)
network.vertex.names(n)=code

However, I am still grappling with two things:
1. How to lookup/convert/match the vertex attribute matrix unique IDs into
the appropriate sequential IDs in the edgelist.
2. How to attach the sequentialized vertex attribute IDs to the network
object.

Assuming attribute_table has 3 columns, [,1] being the non-sequential IDs,
[,2] the sequentialized IDs, and [,3] is the attribute of interest, I
suspect the latter step is something to the effect of sorting on [,2] and
then calling

set.vertex.attribute(n,"attribute_name",attribute_table[,3],v=1:network.size(x))

Thank you for your help ahead of time!

Brian

messages.subject: [statnet_help] ERGMs and co-occurrence networks
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Is there anything special I should take care of when fitting an ERGM to 
a co-occurrence network of political actors (via their common ideas)?

There is no model for weighted networks, so I will have to dichotomize 
edge weights at an arbitrary threshold value, right?

There are also many cliques due to the very nature of a co-occurrence 
network. I suppose I could (1) either model this by including GWDSP and 
GWESP terms (because there are essentially subgroups where every dyad 
has multiple shared partners), or I could (2) argue that the choices of 
ideas in the original two-mode network are actually independent (except 
for covariates), so including network terms for the co-occurrence 
network would be a misspecification - in the latter case, I should 
rather model the co-occurrence network in terms of nodemixing (e.g. same 
actor type, same source of funding etc.). But which makes more sense? 
Intuitively, I would follow the second option.

Thanks for your thoughts about this,

Philip

PS: Btw, I collected the data using my Java software Discourse Network 
Analyzer. I have also written an R package called rDNA which can import 
these networks directly into R. More details on my homepage.

-- 
Philip Leifeld
Max Planck Institute for Research on Collective Goods
http://www.philipleifeld.de

messages.body_plain:
Thanks Vic.  I also forgot to copy this list.

ergm version 2.2-7 is now on CRAN, and it is not much different from  
2.2-6 except that it fixes a couple of bugs.  In particular, one  
potentially important bug, which has been in the code since version  
2.2-3, can reverse the direction of ties in simulated directed  
networks.  Thus, I'd strongly recommend updating to 2.2-7 for anyone  
who depends on directed network simulations (including MCMC-based  
maximum likelihood estimation).


Here, in a nutshell, is the old bug in action:
# using version 2.2-6 now to try to simulate a network with many  
outdegree-3 nodes but few indegree-3 nodes
# by putting a huge positive parameter on odegree(3) and a huge  
negative parameter on idegree(3):
library(ergm)
data(sampson)
mynet <- simulate(samplike ~ odegree(3) + idegree(3), theta0=c(+100,  
-100))
summary(mynet~odegree(3) + idegree(3))
odegree3 idegree3
        0       11

# Now for the same example using version 2.2-7:
library(ergm)
data(sampson)
mynet <- simulate(samplike ~ odegree(3) + idegree(3), theta0=c(+100,  
-100))
summary(mynet~odegree(3) + idegree(3))
odegree3 idegree3
       15        0



Dave

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Re: Attribute lookup/match and import to network object
messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] Re: Attribute lookup/match and import to network object
messages.body_plain:
I worked it out and thought I'd share with the rest of the group if only to
help other newbies. If I botched something terribly or missed the boat
entirely on an easier way to do this, now would be a great time to tell me!
:-)
*
### Reading in directed edgelist to network object. The "network" and "ergm"
libraries don't like networks with non-sequential node names, so if you have
unique IDs, we have to turn them into sequential/ordinal IDs ###
**# Create edgelist matrix named "el" from CSV*
el<-read.csv(file.choose(),header=F)
*# "c" creates a single list of column 1 stacked on top of column 2,
"unique" removes duplicates from this single column, "sort" orders this
column of unique IDs, and "code" is an object where this list of original
IDs can be mapped to sequential/ordinal values*
code<-sort(unique(c(el[,1],el[,2])))
*# Match each of the IDs in the first column of the edgelist to their new
sequential/ordinal number in the "code" mapping list*
el[,1]<-match(el[,1],code)
*# Match each of the IDs in the second column of the edgelist to their new
sequential/ordinal number in the "code" mapping list*
el[,2]<-match(el[,2],code)
*# Import this directed edgelist into a network object.*
n<-network(el,matrix.type="edgelist",directed=T)
*# Rename the vertices back to their original names*
network.vertex.names(n)<-code
*# Re-organize the "code" mapping list to be used for importing attribute
data*
code_frame <- data.frame(code)
*# Give this new object a column name*
colnames(code_frame) <- c('real_id')

*### Reading in nodelist of attributes to network object ###
# Create nodelist matrix named "nl" from CSV assuming you don't have
column/header names*
nl<-read.csv(file.choose(),header=F)
*# Create column/header names*
colnames(nl)<- c('real_id','attribute1')
*# Check to make sure column names are the same*
head(nl)
head(code_frame)
*# Join/merge the "code_frame" mapping object with the "nl" nodelist by
shared "real_id"s*
attributes<-merge(code_frame,nl,by.x='real_id',by.y='real_id')
*# check to make sure attribute vector and code_frame vector are the same
size*
tail(attributes)
tail(code_frame)
*# import each attribute from a column in "attribute" matrix into the
network object "n" starting with the second column which is the first non-id
attribute*
set.vertex.attribute(n, "attribute1", attributes[,2], v=1:network.size(n))
*# check to make sure imported attributes are present in network object*
list.vertex.attribute(n)
*# check to make sure attributes properly imported to network object*
get.vertex.attribute(n, 'attribute1')
